segments: The 18th dynasty.
The Arab kings.
of Egypt,
sent for the Franks.
And many Frankish and Egyptian forces assembled,
and they also crossed over to the western side after Shirkuh.
Then the grandees who were with him advised him,
"We have no other option than to cross to the eastern side,
and go back again to Syria,
because we are not able to withstand the strength of all these.
And if we engage them,
without doubt we know that defeat is closer to us than victory.
And what place of refuge will we have? For behold, the soldiers and peasants and all the people of this land are our enemies."
Then one of the servants of Nur al-Din whose name was Bunqush, a brave young man and a warrior, said to them,
"Believe, all you grandees,
that if you do not engage the enemies,
and you go to Nur al-Din whether victorious or defeated,
so that you might have an excuse {OCR?} before him,
he will cut off all your allowances,
and whatever you have consumed for a long time he will turn around and take back from you.
For whoever shrinks from battle,
let him not be a soldier for kings,
but a peasant,
or let him dwell in houses with women."
And when Shirkuh heard these things, he said,
"My mind is also this."
And Saladin also said,
"I too agree with this."
And then they all agreed to engage.
And the Egyptians and the Franks quickly made an appointment,
and then, though unwilling, they engaged.
Now Shirkuh positioned his brother's son Saladin and all their baggage train in the center of the battle line,
so that their quantity might appear large.
And he commanded them,
"The Franks and the Egyptians think that I am in the center,
and they will spend all their strength on you.
You, however, do not resist them too much,
but quickly turn your back,
and do not be afraid when they pursue you,
because I am behind them."
And when the battle line was drawn up,
Shirkuh chose for himself skilled hunters {experienced warriors} in whose strength and endurance on the field he was confident.
And when the Franks and the Egyptians engaged them,
the center turned their backs,
and the Franks and Egyptians pursued them.
Then Shirkuh pursued the pursuers,
and the fleers also turned back,
and the Egyptians and the Franks were hemmed in the middle,
and a defeat fell upon them. 33 {OCR?}
